verdict.rationale: Reclaim documents its own event-triggered automations. Overbooked smart events are auto-rescheduled, events with a location get travel time, meetings get decompression time, and event hashtags (#reclaim_busy, #reclaim_free, #needs_travel, #nosync) trigger specific scheduler behaviors. These are fixed, built-in triggers that users can toggle or tag, not a rule engine where users write their own event-to-action rules. Missing for 10: user-authored custom rules (arbitrary conditions and actions), any documented rule builder or workflow editor, and independent hands-on corroboration of trigger depth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: If a meeting overbooks another lower-priority smart event, Reclaim automatically reschedules it to the next best time.
Travel Time: auto-add time before and after events with a location.
add the hashtag #reclaim_busy to it. This will tell Reclaim's scheduler to treat that time as busy, despite it being marked as free.
When you add #needs_travel to an event, it will block your default travel time before and after that event.
use the #nosync hashtag in the original event to prevent it from syncing to your target calendar.
